title: 2016 AMC 12A Problem 24
statement: There is a smallest positive real number \(a\) such that there exists a positive real number \(b\) such that all the roots of the polynomial \(x^3-ax^2+bx-a\) are real. In fact, for this value of \(a\) the value of \(b\) is unique. What is this value of \(b?\)

solutions.text:
By Vieta’s formulas, the real roots \(r,s,t\) satisfy \(r+s+t=a,\) \(rs+st+tr=b,\) and \(rst=a,\) so \(r+s+t=rst.\)

The positive product means either all three roots are positive or two are negative. In the latter case write the roots as \(-u,-v,w\) with \(u,v,w\gt0.\) The positive sum forces \(w\gt u+v,\) and then \(b=uv-w(u+v)\lt0,\) a contradiction. Hence all three roots are positive.

By the AM-GM inequality, \(27rst\le(r+s+t)^3=(rst)^3,\) so \(a=rst\ge 3\sqrt3,\) with equality if and only if \(r=s=t=\sqrt3.\) At this smallest \(a,\) \[ \begin{gathered} b=rs+st+tr\\ =3r^2=3\cdot 3=9. \end{gathered} \]

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: If the roots are \(r,s,t,\) then \(r+s+t=a\) and \(rst=a\)
Apply AM-GM to \(r,s,t;\) the minimum \(a\) forces \(r=s=t\)
